one_paragraph_summary: Art's faith-formation chapter, opening with the binary that 'for many men of ambition, faith is an accessory -- useful in ceremony, silent in decision; for Art, faith arrived late and then refused to stay quiet.' Earlier encounters at FEU had planted questions; years of reading and reflection followed; but it was only in the mid-1980s, when he and his wife Elenita joined Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD), that 'faith ceased to be theoretical.' BLD 'demanded vulnerability' -- asking professionals to 'pray aloud, to confess uncertainty, to submit ambition to discernment' -- 'not comfortable, which is precisely why it reshaped him.' He became a servant leader, a marriage-encounter facilitator, a speaker at Life in the Spirit seminars; he read Scripture 'not as metaphor but as instruction'; he came to believe that 'leadership was not granted by election alone -- it was discerned.' Faith pulled him into national service: secretary of the Council of the Laity of the Philippines, delegate to the Second Plenary Council of the Philippines, and ultimately 'improbably -- the only Filipino appointed by Pope John Paul II to the Pontifical Council for the Laity.' The chapter closes with section-to-section narrative continuity: 'the boy who once could not name the Trinity now advised the Vatican on the life of the faithful. Faith had not replaced law in his life. It had disciplined it.'
